subject: Split invoicing proposal for multi-entity orderform — pricing cadence & tax allocation

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecloud.com>

Cc: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@acmecloud.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: ACME review: Order Form redlines (multi-entity billing)

Mateo —

Thanks for sending the updated order form. Procurement reviewed and attached a consolidated redline (ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf). The two main items we need to resolve before procurement approval are:

1) Invoice split across two legal entities: ACME Inc (NA) and ACME EU Sarl (EU). They need invoices addressed to each entity for local tax and audit reasons.
2) Minimum commit phasing: they want a 12-month staircase rather than an upfront annual commit, with invoices aligned to each tranche.

Our finance team has asked for a simple mapping table showing which SKUs/lines will be invoiced to which entity and the associated tax responsibility (reverse-charge vs. withholding). Can Redwood propose the invoice cadence you'd accept?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call Tuesday.

Jordan
Procurement, Acme Cloud

Attachment: ACME_OrderForm_v3_redline.pdf (pdf, 42 KB)

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acmecloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ACME review: Order Form redlines (multi-entity billing)

Jordan —

Appreciate the clear redlines. I reviewed with Finance and Legal (cc'd). High level proposal from Redwood: 

- Split invoicing: We can issue two invoices per payment event: one to ACME Inc (NA) and one to ACME EU Sarl (EU). Each invoice will list only the line items assigned to that entity. We will include the order form reference on both invoices.
- Minimum commit phasing: We can convert the annual commit into 4 quarterly tranches (25% each) for billing purposes, with the following constraints:
  • Tranche invoices are due Net 30 from issuance.
  • If ACME requests a different net term for EU entity due to internal policy, we need written confirmation from procurement and may require a payment guarantee (to avoid inter-entity credit risk).
- Tax allocation: Redwood will show tax as billed party's responsibility by default. For EU reverse-charge cases, Redwood will include the invoice note and supply necessary tax fields; however, if ACME requests Redwood to assume tax gross-up or withholding collection, we need a commercial appendix to capture that allocation.

Action items I suggest:
1) I will draft an "Invoice Allocation Table" (xlsx) mapping SKUs to entity and tranche.
2) Kimberly, can Legal confirm whether the proposed split requires an amendment to the MSA or can be handled in the order form appendix?
3) Karthik, can you confirm we can accept Net 30 on tranche invoices and whether finance needs a PO number per invoice?

If that roadmap works for you, Jordan, I can circulate the mapping + short amendment text by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed-invoice-schedule.xlsx (xlsx, 14 KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 13:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: ACME review: Order Form redlines (multi-entity billing)

Mateo —

Quick read from Legal: the split invoicing itself is operational and can be handled via an Order Form appendix (no MSA amendment required) provided we include:

- A short clause noting that Redwood may issue separate invoices to multiple legal entities identified on the Order Form and that aggregate performance obligations remain with Redwood under the original MSA entity.
- A credit/settlement clause addressing what happens if one entity pays and the other does not (recommend: Redwood reserves right to suspend services for any unpaid invoice; payment default by one entity does not relieve other entity's obligations unless both sign an intercompany settlement).
- Confirmation that tax liability remains with invoiced entity unless a separate tax allocation appendix is agreed. If Acme wants Redwood to bear withholding, that must be priced and documented.

I'll draft 2–3 short paragraph options and mark the redlines in the order form PDF. Mateo, send me the invoice allocation worksheet and I will produce the appendix by EOD tomorrow.

KG
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Looping back — finance is OK with Net 30 on tranche invoices. A few operational notes:

- We need a PO number on each invoice for Acme's AP system; Jordan, can procurement supply a PO per entity per tranche? If not, we can accept a single master PO if Acme's AP will route on their side.
- For the EU reverse-charge, ACME must provide VAT registration numbers for the entities and the legal statement that reverse-charge applies. Otherwise we will include VAT on the invoice.
- If Acme requests Redwood to withhold VAT or assume tax gross-up: pricing team asks for a 3% adder to cover processing and risk — we flagged this as a conditional pricing change.

Jordan/Patricia — once we receive the PO numbers and VAT IDs, Redwood can produce the two-invoice-per-tranche schedule and a short appendix. I'd recommend DocuSign for sign-off to keep audit trail clean.

Thanks,
